The six bullets were parsed with the facade's own parser and their titles equal the six items under the placeholder, so nothing is minted. That is the tracker facade's behaviour, which its own suite pins, not an outcome this spec's slices deliver.

parts.statement: The lint examines the non-exempt locations exercised by the vendor-pattern fixtures and the depth-three fixture.
The two specified skill-relative evals locations are exempt.
All remaining in-scope locations are examined and all remaining evals locations, including src/evals, are exempt.

obligations.source: DEL-D1: "A content test reads every Markdown file under src except those under an evals/ directory."
obligations.statement: The lint reads every Markdown file under src and excludes every file beneath an evals directory.

parts.statement: The specified invented and version-mutated IDs from the six tested naming patterns fail, including the fenced example after its model row is removed.
Unlisted model references outside the six tested naming schemes are also rejected.
Secondary model-table rows in the specified copied, tier-and-effort and two-column layouts fail, with and without outer pipes.
An absent or model-empty routing table fails independently of other file content.
The tested listed-ID prose sentence and fenced example are permitted.

obligations.source: DEL-D1: "a file names a model id the routing table does not list"; "a Markdown table row outside the routing table names a model id, listed or not"; "the routing table is absent or lists no model id"; "Prose and fenced example commands may name a listed id."
obligations.statement: The lint rejects unlisted model references and secondary model inventories, fails closed without a populated routing table, and permits listed IDs in prose and examples.

parts.statement: The actual landed source inventory satisfies those restrictions.

obligations.source: DEL-D1 title: "A lint keeps the routing table the only model inventory"; F1 identifies unguarded example IDs and duplicate inventories as the problem.
obligations.statement: The landed source tree has the routing table as its only model inventory and contains no unlisted model references in the lint's scope.

parts.statement: Extra tier-grid columns, extra models-table columns and a third table are rejected.
The required mappings and metadata remain complete; permitted-column checks do not substitute for required-content checks.

obligations.source: DEL-D1 forbids extra columns and a third table. DEL-D2: "The table carries two things: the model each provider offers at each tier, and per model the price, context and accepted efforts."
obligations.statement: The routing table contains only its two permitted tables and supplies provider-and-tier mappings plus per-model price, context and accepted efforts.

parts.statement: The canonical passage names all four outcomes and source searches establish no second definition.

obligations.source: DEL-D3: "the shared vocabulary is four outcomes named once" and "choosing-a-delegate names the four outcomes any launcher reports".
obligations.statement: Choosing-a-delegate defines the four shared outcomes once, without another source definition.

parts.statement: The tested Codex read-only command uses the documented companion invocation and captures its fixed stdout report in the caller's file.
The tested Codex endings and every documented, script-cross-checked failure signal map to the shared outcomes; caller readers return the five keyed responses.
The tested OpenRouter reader names the clock flags, expiry effects, stopping signal and measured durations.
The remaining contract answers, including permissions, untested worker startup and executable stopping procedures, are supplied correctly.

obligations.source: DEL-D3: "Each launcher skill answers ... whether a run may write or only read; how each kind is started; which of its own signals means which outcome; how a run is bounded and stopped."
obligations.statement: Each launcher skill supplies its whole caller contract, including permissions, startup, outcome classification, bounds and stopping.

parts.statement: The captured minute-26 state is classified correctly and the launched process is identified by PID.
In the delayed scenario, the reader returns the run-specific token and states that the process exited after its recorded exit.
Collection preserves and returns the complete finished report rather than merely its acceptance token.

obligations.source: DEL-D3: "the collection rule for a run that outlives the Bash call"; F7: "the caller waits on the process it launched and on its own capture file"; F8 identifies abandonment of finished reports.
obligations.statement: The Codex skill enables collection of a report after the companion call outlives the Bash call, with supervision of the caller's process and capture file.

parts.statement: The case-insensitive source review finds no raw-binary launch instruction and verifies the named entry point in both callers.

obligations.source: DEL-D3: "Both name the Codex delegation skill's read-only run as the way a Codex reviewer is launched"; F6 identifies the raw-binary ambiguity.
obligations.statement: Source instructions do not direct Codex launches through the raw binary, and the two reviewer callers name the delegation skill's read-only entry point.

parts.statement: Both inspected passages name Edit(<path>).

obligations.source: DEL-D5: "The OpenRouter skill's description and body both require Edit(<path>) for a mandated report file."
obligations.statement: The OpenRouter skill's description and body require the same Edit report-file grant.

parts.statement: Slice C's diffs leave text outside the named passages unchanged.
The broad lens search and the changed-passage inspections establish the specified vocabulary and signal boundaries on the surfaces they examine.
Unchanged passages also contain no forbidden launcher signals or caller vocabulary beyond the searched lens term.

obligations.source: DEL-D3: "No launcher's signals appear in a caller's file. No caller's word, lens included, appears in a launcher's file. Text outside the passages named here does not change."
obligations.statement: Launcher and caller contracts remain separately owned, and slice C changes only the designated passages.

parts.statement: Timeout expiry terminates the tested compliant, resistant, process-group and open-response cases, including the real-clock case.
The specified idle request schedules reset or expire correctly and the tested idle run terminates with reason=idle.
Idle expiry also terminates resistant children, their in-group descendants and runs with open upstream responses.
The five specified expiry and child-exit orderings select the correct reason or preserve the child's own exit.
The specified non-numeric, zero, negative and missing flag-value cases fail before proxy binding.

obligations.source: DEL-D4: "On expiry it ends the child, closes the proxy, and exits 75 with a reason line on stderr"; "Idle means no completion request was forwarded"; invalid values exit 78 before binding.
obligations.statement: OpenRouter timeout and idle expiry terminate the run, close the proxy and report provider failure; invalid bounds are refused before binding.

parts.statement: The tested signal-resistant children and descendants terminate for SIGTERM and SIGINT, with the specified signal-versus-expiry precedence.
Signal-driven stopping also succeeds while an upstream response remains open.

obligations.source: DEL-D4: "A SIGTERM sent to the launcher ends the child even when the child ignores it"; DEL-D3 requires each skill to explain how a run is stopped.
obligations.statement: A runner can stop the OpenRouter run by signaling the launcher, even when the child ignores the signal.

parts.statement: For the tested single-flag and combined-flag invocations, child arguments and environment contain neither clock flag nor its value and otherwise match the unflagged invocation.
The three recorded unflagged inputs preserve their pre-slice child arguments and environment.
Other existing unflagged invocations also preserve their child arguments and environment.

obligations.source: DEL-D4: "The flags are the launcher's own and never reach the child"; the decision adds optional bounds to the existing launcher.
obligations.statement: Clock flags remain launcher-owned and preserve existing child invocation behavior.

parts.statement: The relevant dispatcher settings, including the panel doctrine beside its seat pins, contain the chosen bounds.

obligations.source: DEL-D4: "The dispatching skill chooses the values for its task and stores them alongside its effort and tool settings; the review panel's values live in its doctrine beside its seat pins."
obligations.statement: Dispatchers select and store task-specific clock bounds alongside their effort and tool settings.

parts.statement: The tested reader retrieves low from the OpenRouter skill.
No other artifact independently restates the launcher-specific constraint.

obligations.source: DEL-D2: a launcher-specific constraint "lives in that launcher's skill, once"; section 6: "A whole-artifact read on moonshotai/kimi-k3 runs at low, stated once in the OpenRouter launcher skill."
obligations.statement: The Kimi whole-artifact constraint is low and is owned once by the OpenRouter launcher skill.

parts.statement: Protocol text outside slice C's named passages and outside slice E's renames is preserved in files those slices change.
The remaining slices also preserve the delivery protocol and its existing copies.

obligations.source: DEL-D6: "The delivery protocol and the failover statements stay where they are"; F12 names explicit send, UPDATE and FINAL REPORT in the three agreeing artifacts.
obligations.statement: The existing explicit-send and report-marker delivery protocol stays in its current artifacts.

parts.statement: Failover text outside slice C's named passages and outside slice E's renames is preserved in files those slices change.
Altered passages and the remaining slices preserve the substance and agreement of the failover policies.

obligations.source: DEL-D6 preserves F13, which says any lens may run on any live provider with the substitution recorded and that ac-attack uses the other provider and says so.
obligations.statement: The existing agreeing failover statements retain live-provider substitution and its recording requirements.

parts.statement: The source prose review establishes provider terminology and the four named values.
Every production contracts.json record and ac-attack lens front matter uses the renamed field and a permitted value.
The tested metadata cases with transport, an unknown provider or no provider are refused with coded errors.
The tested claim, ledger and verdict paths use the renamed fields and bumped version, reject the specified obsolete inputs and support the re-keyed scenarios.
Review-verdict's instructional schema documents the bumped version and renamed fields.
Prgroom renders the new-version fixture and names each lens's provider.
Vendor counting uses the actual provider and resolves OpenRouter through the model's vendor prefix.

obligations.source: DEL-D8: "Prose under src says provider"; the panel's and ac-attack's "data and code say provider with those values"; cost includes the verdict version bump and its readers; OpenRouter resolves to its model's vendor.
obligations.statement: Provider terminology and the four provider values propagate through prose, metadata, panel code, verdict schema and prgroom while vendor counting retains its meaning.

parts.statement: The tested cheap-tier low selections pass unchanged in both modes, including the two reader commands and the successful installed-agy lens run.
The specified invalid selection pairs and zzz effort are spawned unchanged.
The tested full variant and bare-model invocations omit an effort flag without adding a default.
Other accepted model-and-effort pairs also pass unchanged in both modes.

obligations.source: DEL-D9: "accepts --model <model> and --effort <level> and hands both to agy as given"; "It composes no id"; omission "adds no level of its own".
obligations.statement: The agy launcher passes model and effort values unchanged, composes no ID and adds no effort when the caller omits it.

parts.statement: The specified exit-1 selection refusals, including the installed-agy invalid pair, reach the caller as exit 78 with the required messages and no reason line.
A missing model or dangling effort flag is refused before spawning.
The tested older-agy unknown-flag failure becomes exit 75 with reason=error and agy's message.
Other non-zero exact-message refusals, successful exits carrying similar text and reworded selection errors follow the specified recognition rule.

obligations.source: DEL-D9 specifies exit 78 with agy's message and no reason line for selection refusal, recognizes a non-zero exit with the error: invalid model selection line, and treats older-flag or reworded errors as exit 75 with reason=error. Its flag interface implies refusal of missing required arguments.
obligations.statement: The agy launcher distinguishes selection refusal, malformed invocation and ordinary agy errors using the documented signals.

parts.statement: The launcher delegates selection knowledge to agy rather than retaining a duplicate list.

obligations.source: DEL-D9: "The launcher holds no list of levels or models"; its rejected validation alternative would create "a second inventory".
obligations.statement: The agy launcher contains no inventory of models or effort levels.

parts.statement: The cheap-tier read-only and worker reader scenarios produce executable separate-flag commands.
The specified source-wide review finds no suffix-composition instruction or effort-only-in-ID statement.

obligations.source: DEL-D9: "Skills teach the two-flag form and do not teach callers to compose an id"; F17 identifies the effort-only-in-ID statement as stale.
obligations.statement: The agy instructions teach separate model and effort flags and stop teaching suffix composition or effort-only-in-ID behavior.

parts.statement: Existing behavior outside the changed selection and refusal contract remains unchanged.

obligations.source: DEL-D9 limits the change to model-and-effort pass-through and selection-refusal handling, says full variant IDs run "as it does today", and reports ordinary agy errors "as it reports any agy error today".
obligations.statement: The agy selection change preserves unrelated existing invocation, exit and stderr behavior.

parts.statement: The specified startup family and spelling cases are refused before binding, and Claude remains refused with the flag.
The tested proxy requests for unpermitted GPT and Gemini selections are denied with and without a pin.
Proxy completion requests selecting Claude are also denied unconditionally.

obligations.source: DEL-D10: "The denylist refuses claude, every gpt- id and every Gemini id"; the flag lifts refusal "never for Claude".
obligations.statement: The OpenRouter denylist refuses Claude unconditionally and GPT or Gemini without a run-specific instruction exception.

parts.statement: The tested flagged refused-family invocation starts, forwards requests and marks its observed ledger lines.
The tested otherwise-allowed model has equal arguments, environment, exit and ledger with or without the flag.
The three reader scenarios distinguish a current explicit instruction from a cheap-run request and an earlier instruction.
Instruction markers also appear on ledger lines from failure paths not exercised by the forwarding scenario.
The exception does not leak into sequential or concurrent runs without their own flag.

obligations.source: DEL-D10: "on that run alone"; "the proxy's ledger lines carry it"; on allowed models "the flag changes nothing and leaves no mark"; the caller passes it only "for the run at hand".
obligations.statement: The instruction flag admits only the instructed run, marks its ledger, has no effect on otherwise allowed models and is used only for the current user's instruction.

parts.statement: Each slice is classified as a feature and promoted before implementation.
The required landing dependency order is followed.
The superseded denylist half of pull request 772 is reworked or closed against slice F.
Delivery adopts the six existing work items without minting replacements.

obligations.source: Section 7: "Each is a feature, and each is promoted with work promote before implementation"; C follows B and D, E lands last after the remaining review-seat pull requests, and F supersedes the denylist half of pull request 772. Continuations: "delivery adopts them and mints nothing".
obligations.statement: Implementation and delivery follow the specified feature promotion, dependency order, superseded-change disposition and existing-item adoption.

ground.reason: DEL-D4 promises that dispatching skills choose timeout values and store them alongside their run settings, with the review panel's values in its doctrine. DEL-B1 to DEL-B7 check optional launcher flags, and DEL-C2 checks a reader's knowledge of those flags. No criterion checks that the promised caller settings exist.

objections.objection: The launcher and skill checks can pass while the review panel has no timeout settings and continues launching unbounded runs.
objections.obligation: The review panel's timeout values live in its doctrine beside its seat pins.

scenario.expect: The checks pass while the promised panel settings are absent; a panel run launched without either optional flag remains unbounded.
scenario.given: A deliverable implements both timeout flags and documents their operation, but leaves the panel's doctrine without timeout values.
scenario.when: The slice B suite and slice C scenarios run.

ground.reason: DEL-V3 promises that a round in flight finishes on the schema version it started on. Its check exercises the new schema, refusal of previous-schema artifacts, and re-keyed scenarios. It names no check that an existing round can still complete through its original version.

objections.objection: Correct rejection of old artifacts can pass acceptance while an unfinished round loses access to the version needed to complete it.
objections.obligation: A round in flight finishes on the version it started on.

scenario.expect: The acceptance checks pass, but the unfinished round's ledger is refused and the promised completion on its original version is unavailable.
scenario.given: A deliverable updates the active scripts to the bumped schema and correctly rejects previous-schema ledgers and verdicts, but retains no runnable original version for an unfinished round.
scenario.when: DEL-V3's suite and re-keyed scenarios run against the new version, then the unfinished round attempts to continue.

ground.reason: DEL-D1 says the test reads every Markdown file under src except files beneath evals. DEL-A1 and DEL-A4 exercise selected locations without checking the complete expected file set.

objections.objection: The lint can omit in-scope files or inspect an exempt location outside the tested directory layouts.

scenario.expect: The lint rejects the exempt file, contrary to DEL-D1.
scenario.given: An implementation passes every check but exempts evals only beneath skill directories. The landed tree contains no src/evals directory.
scenario.when: A Markdown fixture naming an unlisted model is placed directly under src/evals.

ground.reason: DEL-D1 requires failure when a file names an unlisted model ID. DEL-A1 specifies six vendor patterns, without a case for another vendor naming scheme.

objections.objection: An unlisted model from a vendor outside the six tested patterns can pass.

scenario.expect: The lint exits successfully despite the unlisted model ID.
scenario.given: Every check passes with an ID recognizer covering only Claude, GPT, Gemini, Kimi and GLM spellings.
scenario.when: An in-scope Markdown sentence names deepseek/deepseek-v4, which is absent from the routing table.

ground.reason: DEL-D1 promises that the routing table remains the only model inventory. DEL-A2 observes the lint's successful exit and its reported files, rather than independently checking the landed inventory.

objections.objection: The landed tree can contain inventory drift that the lint fails to recognize.

scenario.expect: It reports success although the source inventory violates DEL-D1.
scenario.given: Every check passes, including DEL-A2, while a landed Markdown file contains an unlisted ID outside the lint's recognized vendor patterns.
scenario.when: The landed-head lint runs.

ground.reason: No passage outside the criteria promises a successful gate invocation or a file-list report as the deliverable. DEL-A2's check establishes those artifacts without establishing the inventory property it states.

objections.objection: DEL-A2's check discharges no inventoried part.

scenario.expect: The check completes without independently determining whether the source inventory satisfies any of those obligations.
scenario.given: The obligations concern the lint's coverage, rejection behavior and the source inventory.
scenario.when: DEL-A2 observes a zero exit and a reported file list.

ground.reason: DEL-D2 says the table carries each provider's model at each tier and each model's price, context and accepted efforts. DEL-A7 checks forbidden additions, rather than completeness of these required contents.

objections.objection: The routing table can lose required mappings or metadata while retaining only permitted columns.

scenario.expect: The promised context data is absent, although no forbidden column or third table exists.
scenario.given: Every check passes after the landed models table loses its context column while retaining model IDs and the columns used by the reader scenarios.
scenario.when: A dispatcher reads the table for a model's context capacity.

ground.reason: DEL-D3 requires each launcher skill to answer permission, startup, signal and stopping questions for its run kinds. The scenarios cover selected read-only commands and signals, without checking all those answers.

objections.objection: A launcher skill can remain incomplete about permissions, worker startup or an executable stopping procedure.

scenario.expect: The caller can identify the process but cannot obtain the promised stopping procedure from the skill.
scenario.given: Every check passes and the Codex reader correctly names the running process's PID, but the skill supplies no procedure for signaling that process.
scenario.when: A caller holding only that skill needs to stop the run.

ground.reason: DEL-D3 promises collection of a backgrounded run's output. DEL-C8 keys acceptance on a token and an after-exit statement, without comparing the returned report with the complete captured report.

objections.objection: A reader can discard the findings and return only the acceptance token.

scenario.expect: DEL-C8 passes while the report itself has not been collected and returned.
scenario.given: Every check passes and the delayed stub emits a report containing several findings and the generated token.
scenario.when: The reader waits for exit and answers with only the token and a statement that the process exited.

ground.reason: DEL-D3 says no launcher signals appear in a caller's file and no caller vocabulary appears in a launcher file. DEL-C9 checks these boundaries only in changed passages, apart from its broader searches for lens and outcome definitions.

objections.objection: Forbidden cross-boundary content can remain in an unchanged passage.

scenario.expect: The paragraph escapes those checks while violating the file-wide ownership boundary.
scenario.given: Every check passes, but an unchanged caller paragraph quotes a launcher-specific reason line outside the passages slice C modifies.
scenario.when: The reviewer performs DEL-C9's changed-passage checks and its searches for lens and outcome definitions.

ground.reason: DEL-D4 requires expiry to end the child and close the proxy. DEL-B1 exercises resistant children and open upstream responses for timeout expiry; DEL-B2 does not require those cases for idle expiry.

objections.objection: Idle expiry can fail to terminate a resistant run or close an open upstream response.

scenario.expect: The child or proxy survives, although the compliant idle scenarios and all timeout scenarios pass.
scenario.given: Every check passes, but the idle handler uses a weaker shutdown path than the timeout handler.
scenario.when: Idle expiry occurs after a forwarded request remains open and the child ignores SIGTERM.

ground.reason: DEL-D3 requires stopping guidance and DEL-D4 commits to SIGTERM ending even a resistant child. DEL-B6 does not exercise signal-driven shutdown while an upstream response remains open.

objections.objection: An open upstream response can obstruct the launcher's signal-driven stopping path.

scenario.expect: The run remains alive despite the promised stopping behavior.
scenario.given: Every check passes, but the signal handler waits for an open upstream response before completing child termination.
scenario.when: SIGTERM reaches a launcher whose child ignores the signal and whose upstream response remains open.

ground.reason: DEL-D4 adds optional launcher-owned flags. DEL-B4 compares unchanged default launching for three recorded inputs; it does not establish preservation for other existing inputs.

objections.objection: A default invocation outside the recorded fixtures can receive changed child arguments or environment.

scenario.expect: The child's arguments differ from the pre-slice launcher.
scenario.given: Every check passes, but the new argument parser changes an existing tool-grant combination absent from the three pre-slice fixtures.
scenario.when: That invocation runs with neither clock flag.

ground.reason: DEL-D4 explicitly places task-selected timeout values alongside effort and tool settings, with the panel's values beside its seat pins. No criterion checks those settings or their location.

objections.objection: The launcher can gain clock flags while callers retain no task-specific bounds.

scenario.expect: The run starts without the promised stored bounds.
scenario.given: Every check passes, including readers correctly naming the flags.
scenario.when: The panel dispatches using doctrine that contains no timeout or idle-timeout values beside its seat pins.

ground.reason: DEL-D2 places launcher-specific constraints in that launcher's skill once, and section 6 says the Kimi whole-artifact low setting is stated once there. DEL-C2 checks retrieval from one skill, without checking uniqueness.

objections.objection: The Kimi constraint can remain duplicated in a caller artifact.

scenario.expect: The correct answer is returned while the promised single ownership remains violated.
scenario.given: Every check passes and the OpenRouter skill correctly states low, while an unchanged panel passage independently repeats the same Kimi whole-artifact constraint.
scenario.when: DEL-C2's reader consults only the OpenRouter skill.

ground.reason: DEL-D6 says the delivery protocol stays where it is. DEL-C7 and DEL-V6 protect certain diffs, but no criterion checks preservation across the remaining slices.

objections.objection: The explicit-send or report-marker protocol can be removed outside the protected diffs.

scenario.expect: They accept the model refusal and flag behavior while the preserved delivery protocol has changed.
scenario.given: Every check passes, but slice F also removes the explicit-send instruction from a delegation artifact.
scenario.when: The slice F checks run.

ground.reason: DEL-D6 preserves the failover statements. DEL-C3 checks outcome-to-response answers, without checking that an altered caller passage still permits live-provider substitution and records it.

objections.objection: Caller wording can preserve claim reasons while losing the agreed failover policy.

scenario.expect: The keyed answer passes although the preserved substitution policy is absent.
scenario.given: Every check passes, but an edited harvest passage still maps provider failure to transport-error while removing permission to run the lens on another live provider.
scenario.when: The provider fails and the reader answers DEL-C3's claim-reason question.

ground.reason: DEL-D8 requires the real contracts and lens metadata to use provider. DEL-V2 specifies refusal cases, without explicitly checking every production metadata record.

objections.objection: Parser fixtures can pass while a production contract or lens retains transport.

scenario.expect: The promised provider field is absent and the parser may reject the production record.
scenario.given: Every check passes using renamed fixtures, but a production contracts.json entry retains transport: codex.
scenario.when: The real panel loads that contract.

ground.reason: DEL-D8 includes the verdict-envelope version bump and its readers. DEL-V3 states that review-verdict documents the new schema, but its specified check does not identify an observation of that documentation.

objections.objection: Code can adopt the new schema while review-verdict still teaches the old fields.

scenario.expect: The caller produces an obsolete envelope despite the promised documented version bump.
scenario.given: Every suite and scenario passes with the new code and fixtures, while review-verdict's schema documentation retains transport and the previous version.
scenario.when: A caller follows that documentation to construct a verdict.

ground.reason: DEL-D9 requires model and effort values to pass through unchanged. DEL-G1, DEL-G2, DEL-G7 and DEL-G8 cover specified pairs and omissions, without a successful high-effort pair.

objections.objection: An accepted high-effort selection can be altered while all specified selections pass.

scenario.expect: The spawn receives low instead of the caller's unchanged high value.
scenario.given: Every check passes, but the launcher changes an explicitly supplied high effort to low.
scenario.when: A worker runs with --model gemini-3.8-flash --effort high.

ground.reason: DEL-D9 recognizes selection refusal by a non-zero exit with the specified message and treats reworded refusals as ordinary errors. DEL-G2 uses exit 1 and DEL-G9 uses an unknown-flag message.

objections.objection: Other non-zero selection-refusal exits or reworded refusals can be misclassified.

scenario.expect: The first becomes a provider error and the second becomes a refused invocation, contrary to DEL-D9.
scenario.given: Every check passes, but the recognizer requires exit 1 and separately treats any message containing model and invalid as a selection refusal.
scenario.when: One stub exits 2 with the exact selection-refusal line, and another emits a reworded invalid-pairing error.

ground.reason: DEL-D9 says the launcher holds no list of levels or models. Passing zzz unchanged does not establish the absence of a list.

objections.objection: The launcher can contain a duplicate inventory that includes the test values.

scenario.expect: The launcher rejects the value using its duplicate inventory instead of delegating selection to agy.
scenario.given: Every check passes with a launcher-maintained list containing low, medium, high, zzz and all fixture model names.
scenario.when: agy gains another accepted level and the caller supplies it.

ground.reason: DEL-D9 confines the change to selection pass-through and refusal handling while preserving existing invocation and error behavior. DEL-G4 observes only the existing suite's successful completion.

objections.objection: Existing behavior outside the old suite's assertions can change unnoticed.

scenario.expect: The spawned arguments or resulting stderr differ from the preserved behavior.
scenario.given: Every check passes, but an existing prompt or tool-grant combination not exercised by the suite is parsed differently.
scenario.when: A caller repeats that previously valid invocation.

ground.reason: No passage outside the criteria makes a successful unchanged test suite the deliverable. DEL-G4's gate observation establishes neither an argv nor an exit-code nor a stderr preservation case.

objections.objection: DEL-G4's check discharges no inventoried part.

scenario.expect: The gate result is obtained without an identified observation establishing one of the promised preservation behaviors.
scenario.given: The document's obligations concern launcher behavior and its instructional artifacts.
scenario.when: The existing suite completes successfully without the specified forbidden-effort test.

ground.reason: DEL-D10 says the denylist refuses Claude and the flag never lifts that refusal. DEL-F1 and DEL-F3 check startup selection; DEL-F5 checks proxy requests only for GPT and Gemini.

objections.objection: A proxy started on an allowed model can accept a completion request selecting Claude.

scenario.expect: The proxy forwards the request despite the unconditional Claude refusal.
scenario.given: Every check passes, but the proxy's request denylist omits Claude.
scenario.when: An unpinned run started on an allowed model submits a completion request for a Claude model.

ground.reason: DEL-D10 requires ledger lines to carry the flag whenever it admitted the run. DEL-F2 specifies a fake child and upstream but no failed-request ledger case.

objections.objection: Error ledger lines can omit the instruction marker.

scenario.expect: That line omits user-instructed, preventing the promised audit from identifying the admitted run.
scenario.given: Every check passes and successful forwarded requests carry user-instructed.
scenario.when: An instructed GPT run encounters an upstream error that writes a separate ledger line.

ground.reason: DEL-D10 lifts refusal on that run alone. The flag criteria do not require a sequential or concurrent isolation check.

objections.objection: An instruction exception can persist into another run.

scenario.expect: The second run is admitted even though the exception belonged only to the first run.
scenario.given: Every isolated check passes, but an instructed run persists an admission exception in shared state.
scenario.when: A second GPT run starts without --user-instructed against that state.

ground.reason: Section 7 says each slice is a feature promoted with work promote before implementation. No criterion observes feature classification or promotion timing.

objections.objection: All implementation checks can pass without the required promotion.

scenario.expect: The criteria accept work that violates the stated execution contract.
scenario.given: All artifact, suite and reader checks pass.
scenario.when: A slice is implemented before its feature is promoted.

ground.reason: Section 7 requires C after B and D, and E last after the remaining review-seat pull requests. No criterion checks landing order.

objections.objection: The final artifacts can pass while the required dependency order is violated.

scenario.expect: The stated ordering guarantee was violated despite the passing final tree.
scenario.given: All checks pass on the completed combined tree.
scenario.when: E lands before a remaining review-seat pull request, or C lands before D.

ground.reason: Section 7 says F supersedes the denylist half of pull request 772, which is reworked or closed against it. No criterion observes that disposition.

objections.objection: The superseded denylist change can remain live and contradictory.

scenario.expect: The promised rework or closure has not occurred.
scenario.given: Every slice F check passes.
scenario.when: F lands while pull request 772 retains its superseded denylist change and remains open without rework.

ground.reason: Continuations says delivery adopts the existing work items and mints nothing. No criterion checks delivery's tracker effects.

objections.objection: Delivery can create duplicate work items.

scenario.expect: New items are minted contrary to the continuation contract.
scenario.given: All implementation checks pass and the six named work items already exist.
scenario.when: Delivery creates replacement slice items instead of adopting the existing ones.

ground.reason: DEL-C2 keys the scenario answer on "the two durations", but the passage the reader must cite (F9, which DEL-D4 orders recorded as facts) states three measured durations: 4 to 9 minutes for an inline read, 27 minutes for a repository read, and 67 minutes for the run that ended inside a thinking block. The criterion never says which two of the three are keyed, so the wording admits materially different keyed answers.

objections.objection: The acceptance authority (the key) can be written as "4–9 minutes and 27 minutes" or as any pair including the 67-minute figure, and a reader citing the unhealthy 67-minute run as one of the two durations can be judged either correct (it is a measured duration recorded in F9) or incorrect (the key picked the two healthy figures).
objections.obligation: DEL-C2: the reader states the measured durations of F9

scenario.expect: The run fails against the key even though both numbers the reader gave are measured durations the skill records, while a key written to include 67 minutes would have passed the same answer — the criterion's wording permits both keys
scenario.given: The openrouter-claude-subagent skill recording F9's durations as facts (4–9 min, 27 min, and the 67-minute run), and a committed key for scenario C2e naming "the two durations" as 4–9 minutes and 27 minutes
scenario.when: A scenario-protocol run asks the reader, holding only that skill, for the measured durations, and the reader answers with the 27-minute and 67-minute figures

ground.reason: DEL-B6 specifies that on SIGTERM/SIGINT the launcher "exits within ten seconds", and specifies "reason=signal" only for the one-tick coincidence case; it never fixes the exit code, nor whether a reason line is emitted, for the plain signal case. DEL-D4 likewise says the SIGTERM kill happens but assigns no exit contract. Yet DEL-C3 requires every documented signal to map to one of the four outcomes, which presupposes a defined exit behaviour. The wording leaves the exit code and reason-line decision open, and each reading produces a different outcome mapping under DEL-C3.

objections.objection: An implementation exiting 75 with "[run] reason=signal" and one exiting 143 (128+SIGTERM) with no reason line both satisfy DEL-B6's plain-signal case, but they force different outcome classifications in DEL-C3's committed signal list (provider-style failure vs. caller-signalled stop), so two conformant implementations yield different verdicts against the same criteria.
objections.obligation: DEL-B6: signal delivered to the launcher ends the child and the launcher exits

scenario.expect: Under exit 143 with no reason line the signal cannot be keyed to the documented "reason=signal" mapping, while a sibling implementation exiting 75 with reason=signal keys it as "stop" — both launchers pass DEL-B6 but produce diverging DEL-C3 verdicts
scenario.given: The slice-B launcher built to DEL-B1–B7, with DEL-B6 implemented to exit 143 and emit no reason line on a plain SIGTERM
scenario.when: Slice C commits its DEL-C3 signal list cross-checked against the launcher's exit codes and reason lines, and a scenario asks a harvest.md reader the response for the launcher's plain-SIGTERM ending

ground.reason: DEL-C3's cross-check runs in one direction only: a signal the script emits but the skill omits fails the criterion, but nothing checks the reverse. Asked 'what if the skill documents a signal that never occurs', no criterion answers — the scenario list is 'keyed on the reason names in force' and the failure trigger covers only script-to-skill drift, so a stale or invented signal in a launcher skill (e.g. an exit code the launcher can never produce, left behind after slice B or D changes the script) passes every check while the skill teaches the reader to expect it.

objections.objection: A launcher skill documenting a failure signal its launcher never emits passes DEL-C3, so a reader of that skill maps a phantom outcome the run can never produce, and the drift the criterion exists to catch survives in the documented-to-emitted direction.

scenario.expect: the criterion fails, because the skill teaches a signal no run can produce — but the check only fails on signals the script emits and the skill omits, so it passes
scenario.given: slice C landed, and a launcher skill documents a signal (an exit code or reason line) that the launcher script at the slice's head never emits
scenario.when: DEL-C3's check runs: the committed signal list is cross-checked against the script's exit codes and reason lines

ground.reason: Asked 'what if it runs at the same time / interleaved': DEL-V3 refuses any ledger or verdict of the previous schema version with a coded error, and its stated purpose is 'so a round in flight finishes on the version it started on' — but no criterion tests that an in-flight round can actually finish once the bumped tools are live. The suite covers the refusals and one run of the re-keyed scenarios, never the interleaving of an old-version round with the new-version tools.

objections.objection: A review round that claimed its lenses under the old schema version cannot complete after slice E lands mid-round: its remaining claims, ledger and final verdict are all previous-version artifacts the new dispatch_gate.py and review-verdict refuse, so the round is stranded — the opposite of the outcome the criterion's own text states as the reason for refusing migration.

scenario.expect: the round finishes on the version it started on, as DEL-V3 states — instead each old-version artifact is refused with a coded error, and no criterion checks the round can ever close
scenario.given: a review round opened and partially claimed under the pre-bump verdict schema, with lenses still to run
scenario.when: slice E ships mid-round, and the round's remaining `dispatch_gate.py claim` calls and its final verdict are issued under the previous schema version
